newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain court overturns jury acquittal of cop killer.
newsitem.headline: Spain court overturns jury acquittal of cop killer.

text.p: A Spanish court on Friday overturned the controversial jury acquittal of a man linked to ETA guerrillas who had confessed to killing two police officers.

The court, in Spain's Basque country, ordered a re-trial for Mikel Otegi whose acquittal in March sparked a national outcry. A jury found he was not responsible for his actions when he shot dead the two officers at a farm in Itasondo in northern Spain in 1995.
In a review of the trial, the court concluded that there had been "a significant flaw in the deliberations and voting among jurors".
"The jury did not complete the job they were given..." the court said in its conclusions. The court said the case would be re-tried with a new jury.
Basque politicians said the decision highlighted the deficiencies in Spain's jury law and called for vital reforms.
The previous trial was riddled with problems.
Basque officials and judges said they suspected jurors had acquitted the 23-year-old, an alleged member of radical youth group Jarrai with links to ETA separatist guerrillas, for fear of reprisals.
From the beginning the court had trouble finding jurors who did not fear retribution by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
Spanish newspaper El Mundo reported that during the trial jurors had not understood many of the questions asked of them and did not realise that their decision was final.
Otegi had confessed to the killings but said in his defence that he had suffered a mental blackout at the time.
The verdict led to calls for a ban on the use of juries -- a relatively new concept in Spain introduced in 1995.
The government responded by initiating a study on possible reforms of the jury law, and a decision is expected to be announced in the coming weeks.
